name: Novalign Posture-Active Work Shirt
description:
A fitted button-front work shirt in a grey-blue ripstop cotton-analog, cut for people who spend their day at standing desks, in server rooms, or doing light physical work in corporate environments. The fabric has a subtle stretch in four directions and is treated to resist minor stains and static buildup. The collar is a relaxed point-collar — less formal than a dress shirt, more structured than a polo. There are two chest pockets with snap closures and a discreet sleeve pocket for a stylus or ID card.

The Novalign designation refers to the shirt's actual tech feature: thin conductive threads woven into the upper back and shoulder panels connect to a small module at the collar that delivers light haptic feedback when your posture deviates from a calibrated baseline. It's subtle — a gentle pressure, not a shock. Most wearers turn it off after a week. But the shirt itself is good enough that they keep wearing it anyway. Common in Tier 3 and 4 office-tech environments.
functionality: Embedded posture-monitoring haptic feedback system in the upper back and shoulder panels; connects to BCI or standalone collar module. Calibrates to user baseline over 72 hours. Most wearers disable the haptic function.
what_it_says: You have a job that involves sitting at something for eight hours, and someone — maybe you, maybe your employer — thought posture correction was worth the premium.
worn_by: anyone whose employer subsidized the purchase
story_hooks: The posture data collected by Novalign shirts is stored — the company's privacy policy is long and deliberately vague about what 'aggregate wellness analytics' means.
A corporate espionage angle: someone has found a way to use the haptic module as a short-range transmitter.
A Tier 3 worker discovers their employer has been accessing their Novalign data to flag 'stress events' during the workday — and acting on that information in performance reviews.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, utilitarian work shirt with athletic undertones. The fitted silhouette skews modern-professional rather than traditional business—built for movement and long hours at a desk or on your feet. The grey-blue tone reads as practical and neutral, neither corporate formality nor street wear.
physical_description.fit: Fitted through the torso with tapered sleeves; cut to accommodate slight movement without excess fabric. Designed to sit comfortably over light augmentation or body-worn tech without bunching.
physical_description.primary_material: Grey-blue ripstop cotton-analog with four-directional stretch. Treated for stain resistance and static suppression.
physical_description.texture: Subtle diagonal ripstop weave visible under light; the fabric has a slight sheen from the treatment. Smooth to the touch but with tactile grip—not slippery. Micro-ribbed in places where conductive thread is embedded.
physical_description.color_scheme: Muted grey-blue base (hex: #5a7a8c or similar). No visible patterns; the ripstop weave creates understated visual texture. Snaps and collar trim in brushed silver or charcoal.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap buttons down the front placket (quieter than traditional buttons, better for office environments). Snap closures on both chest pockets and the discreet sleeve pocket.
distinctive_features: Two chest pockets with snap closures
Hidden sleeve pocket on right arm for stylus or ID card
Embedded conductive thread pattern visible as faint gridlines across upper back and shoulders
Small circular haptic feedback module at collar (matte black, roughly 1.5cm diameter)
Interior neck tag with Novalign branding and calibration QR code
Reinforced shoulder and upper back panels where tech threads concentrate
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 functional. Mid-range corp-tech apparel. Accessible to working-class professionals but not luxury.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by office workers, server technicians, data analysts, facilities managers—people who exist in the grey zone between desk and physical labor. Signals someone who treats their body as a tool and invests in comfort tech. Pragmatic, not fashionable.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn in—creases at the elbows and collar from daily use. Possible faint stain marks that the treatment has minimized. The haptic module might show micro-scratches. Overall: functional and lived-in, not pristine.
